verifier_note: Checked all 10 recipes against retrieved pages only (never memory): doc.rust-lang.org/stable (1.98.1 banner confirmed on every std/core page), the Reference, the Nomicon, the Book, docs.rs at the exact pinned versions (rayon 1.12.0, rayon-core 1.13.0, crossbeam-channel 0.5.17, tokio 1.53.1, rapier3d-f64 0.35.3), the raw dimforge/rapier CHANGELOG.md at tag v0.35.3, and two rustc platform-support pages, plus si-rpg-engine's solver/src/lib.rs, rapier_law.rs, Cargo.toml and FLAGS.md via read-only gh api on main. Every one of the 57 checks[] entries was independently recompiled and run through scripts/compile_oracle.py on rustc 1.98.1 (including the wasm32-unknown-unknown target via the real oracle, and the rapier3d_f64-gated host checks against the same =0.35.3+enhanced-determinism dependency the oracle and the solver both pin) — all 57 matched their claimed expect/error_codes/lints/stdout/exit_code exactly, with zero mismatches, including the 6 checks carrying the `no_warnings`/`wasm_no_imports` gates the input was regenerated to restore (re-run explicitly after that correction landed). I also wrote and ran several of my own counter-examples beyond the given checks (an ordering-through-a-variable probe, a no_std atomics-link probe) to independently stress the two most decisive claims. The one systemic weakness: citation precision on secondary/adjacent-version pages. Recipe 7's 'wasm32-wasip1-threads platform support' source is cited for enabling atomics/bulk-memory/mutable-globals AND for '--shared-memory' linking AND a 'thread-spawn' import, but a full-page text scan of that exact rustc page (twice) turns up only the first group plus --import-memory/--export-memory (an LLVM<16 note) — '--shared-memory' and 'thread-spawn' never appear there, even though both are true facts about wasi-threads that I could not source from THIS citation. The same recipe also leans on a rapier.rs user-guide page it explicitly labels 'labelled 0.36' (i.e. not the pinned 0.35.3) as secondary corroboration for its central determinism claim, which the recipe itself flags as unmeasured vendor marketing rather than passing it off as equivalent evidence — good practice, but it is the same secondary-source pattern. No source was unreachable, no API or lint name was stale or misnamed anywhere in the lane, and no check tested a different fact than its prose asserted.
